extraction_notes: CACI is a defense IT services / intel mission-support prime. Unlike the YSS/IONQ short-thesis archetype, the 10-K narrative is built on capability themes (SIGINT, EW, C-UAS, free-space optical communications, photonics, special operations support) and a portfolio of recent technology acquisitions (Ascent Vision Technologies, Photon Research-type FSO/photonics, CSfC, OSINT), rather than naming specific Pentagon Program Elements (PEs) or DoD programs of record by name. The filing also makes broad DoD customer-concentration assertions (DoD = 69.8% of FY2022 revenue) and a top-10-contract concentration (35.7%). For J-Book divergence testing, the only DoD-program-adjacent claims are CAPABILITY-LEVEL (C-UAS, FSO, EW, SIGINT) rather than program-element-level. We therefore extract: (a) capability/mission-area claims that would be load-bearing if their underlying PEs were being zeroed; (b) DoD-customer-concentration claims; (c) acquisition-coherence claims around AVT/Photon-FSO/CSfC; and (d) control non-J-Book claims (international ops, GSA schedule, top-10 concentration). NOTE: pentagon_jbook corpus covers ~410 PEs heavily seeded for emerging-tech / quantum / small-sat / autonomy short cases (RCAT, UMAC, ONDS, AIRO, KTOS, RKLB, IONQ, etc.) and is NOT seeded for CACI's classified IC / SIGINT / mission-support PE space — so NOT_FOUND results here are expected and indicate corpus coverage gap rather than a real signal.

claims.claim_text: CACI is at the forefront of developing free space optical (FSO) communications and long-range sensing using lasers, and acquired multi-domain photonics technologies for FSO communications during fiscal 2022.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: We are at the forefront of developing technologies that meet the challenges of 5G wireless communications both on and off the battlefield, mmWave, and the use of lasers for free space optical communications and long-range sensing. ... During fiscal 2022, CACI completed four acquisitions ... multi-domain photonics technologies for free-space optical (FSO) communications, and commercial solutions for classified (CSfC) security technologies.

claims.claim_text: CACI provides full-spectrum cyber, electronic warfare, and Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) solutions as a core C4ISR/Cyber/Space capability area.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: Our software-defined, full-spectrum cyber, electronic warfare, and counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) solutions provide electromagnetic spectrum advantage and deliver precision effects against national security threats.

claims.claim_text: CACI provides multi-domain SIGINT, resilient communications, FSO communications, EW, cyber operations, and 5G/RF spectrum capabilities to Mission customers — implying a forward revenue dependency on DoD signals-intelligence and spectrum-awareness program lines.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: Additional examples of Mission technology include: Developing and deploying multi-domain offerings for signals intelligence, resilient communications, free space optical communications, electronic warfare including Counter-UAS, cyber operations, and Radio Frequency (RF) and 5G spectrum awareness, agility and usage.

claims.claim_text: In fiscal 2021 CACI acquired Ascent Vision Technologies (AVT), which specializes in Electro-Optical Infrared (EO/IR) payloads, On-Board Computer Vision Processing and Counter-UAS solutions — positioning CACI on DoD C-UAS programs of record.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: During fiscal 2021, CACI completed the acquisition of Ascent Vision Technologies (AVT). AVT specializes in Electro-Optical Infrared payloads, On-Board Computer Vision Processing and counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) solutions.

claims.claim_text: Department of Defense agencies generated 69.8% of CACI's total revenue in fiscal 2022 and 69.3% in fiscal 2021. CACI expects federal government contracts to continue to be the primary source of revenue for the foreseeable future.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.object_value: DoD = 69.8% of FY2022 revenues; total federal = 94.8%
claims.source_quote: revenues from federal government contracts, either as a prime contractor or a subcontractor, accounting for 94.8% and 95.5% of our total revenues in fiscal 2022 and 2021, respectively. Specifically, we generated 69.8% and 69.3% of our total revenues in fiscal 2022 and 2021, respectively, from contracts with agencies of the DoD. We expect that federal government contracts will continue to be the primary source of our revenues for the foreseeable future.

claims.claim_text: For fiscal 2022 CACI's top-ten revenue-producing contracts (many comprising multiple task orders) accounted for 35.7% of revenues, or $2.2 billion.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: For fiscal 2022, the top ten revenue-producing contracts, many of which consist of many task orders, accounted for 35.7% of our revenues, or $2.2 billion.

claims.claim_text: CACI provides special operations services (including counterterrorism training) and intelligence/special-operations mission support — implying revenue from SOCOM program lines.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: Our federal business includes the maintenance of global networks and the provision of special operations services (e.g., counterterrorism training) ... mission support expertise such as intelligence and special operations support.

claims.claim_text: Domestic Operations represented 96.9% of total revenues in fiscal 2022 (control claim — geographic mix, not J-Book-grounded).
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: Domestic Operations represented 96.9%, 97.1%, and 97.1% of our total revenues for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, June 30, 2021, and June 30, 2020, respectively.

claims.claim_text: CACI completed eight acquisitions over fiscal 2020-2022 to add OSINT, satellite communications, FSO/photonics, CSfC, EO/IR, and C-UAS capabilities — a rollup thesis tying multiple acquired hardware/photonics businesses to DoD program-of-record exposure.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: During the past three fiscal years, we completed a total of eight acquisitions, including: During fiscal 2022, CACI completed four acquisitions that provide mission and enterprise technology to sensitive government customers. Their capabilities include open source intelligence solutions, specialized cyber, satellite communications, multi-domain photonics technologies for free-space optical (FSO) communications, and commercial solutions for classified (CSfC) security technologies.

claims.claim_text: Control claim (non-J-Book): CACI sells extensively through GSA schedule contracts and other government-wide acquisition contracts (GWACs/IDIQs), implying access via existing vehicles rather than program-of-record concentration.
claims.subject: CACI
claims.source_quote: Budgetary pressures and changes in the procurement process have caused many government customers to increasingly purchase goods and services through IDIQ contracts, GSA schedule contracts and other government-wide acquisition contracts.
